newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-BEHIND THE SCENES IN SESTRIERE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-BEHIND THE SCENES IN SESTRIERE.

text.p: The following is a collection of behind the scenes incidents from the first week of the Alpine skiing world championships:

World Cup downhill champion Luc Alphand, catching sight of the world championships' rotund elephant mascot 'Annifant', could not resist a dig at beefy rival and defending world champion Patrick Ortlieb of Austria.
"I'm leaving with my elephant, with Patrick Ortlieb," he said after a news conference in the French team's hotel, tucking a large cut-out of the symbol under his arm.
Argentine television cameras have been following keenly every event so far in Sestriere.
However a producer for the private station admitted that viewers in the south American country would not be able to follow the action for another couple of months.
The Argentine summer is in full swing and the skiing coverage will be kept on ice for the winter.
Mexico's sole entrant Hubertus von Hohenlohe, a championships veteran and regular tail-ender, is keeping the day job going while on the piste.
A music producer in Austria, he was heard singing a few bars from "Don't Cry For Me Argentina" as he headed away from the finish area after a tiring training session.
British skier Andrew Freshwater found himself cast as "Braveheart" after losing two front teeth and cracking a third after catching a slalom pole in the face.
Team mate Graham Bell said that the young Scot underwent two hours of surgery without anaesthetic after the combined slalom, with the dentist whispering "Braveheart" to encourage him.
Austrian Mario Reiter needed more than a few whispers of encouragement after winning a combined bronze.
It took him two hours, one can of beer, two bottles of water, six fruit juices and three attempts to provide a urine sample in the mandatory post-race dope test.
He finally emerged in triumph six minutes before midnight and headed to the Austria House. For another drink.
The weather has been everything the organisers could desire with sun and cloudless blue skies.
For those looking for the full summer experience, one sponsor laid out beach pedalos, canoes and trees with fake bananas in a central pedestrian square to promote a summer collection of watches.
There was even a "snow volleyball" court.
